acceptance_criteria.criterion: Running `./menu.sh` (Unix) or `menu.cmd` (Windows) displays a numbered menu of developer tasks.
Menu options 1–6 correctly dispatch to their respective commands via `passthru()`.
Option 3 (Tests) presents a sub-prompt for a filter pattern; empty input runs all tests.
The menu loops after each action completes; selecting `0` exits cleanly.
If `vendor/` is missing, `composer install` is run automatically before showing the menu.

summary: Created tools/menu.php — interactive numbered developer menu with vendor pre-flight, menu loop, and full dispatch for all 6 options (plus option 0 to exit).
Option 3 (Tests) sub-prompts for an optional filter pattern; empty input runs the full suite via `composer test`, non-empty runs `composer test-filter -- <pattern>`.
Created menu.sh (Unix launcher) — thin bash wrapper that cd's to the project root and invokes `php tools/menu.php`.
Created menu.cmd (Windows launcher) — thin batch wrapper using `cd /d %~dp0` and invokes `php tools/menu.php`.
PHP syntax verified clean with `php -l`. File uses `declare(strict_types=1)` and no `[]` array literals.

comments.note: tools/menu.php uses escapeshellarg() on the setup-local.php path and the test filter value — this is defensive and correct. If the project root ever contains spaces, the path quoting will prevent breakage.

The `composer test-filter -- <pattern>` invocation passes the filter after `--` to separate Composer args from PHPUnit args, matching the existing `test-filter` script definition in composer.json (`php vendor/bin/phpunit --no-progress --filter`). This is consistent with how the script is defined.
No observations — code in the touched files is clean and consistent with the patterns established in tools/setup-local.php and tools/include/cli-utilities.php.

summary: Build & Runtime: php -l confirms no syntax errors in tools/menu.php. All three files are present (tools/menu.php, menu.sh, menu.cmd).
AC1 (menu display): showMenu() renders options 1–6 plus 0; menu.sh and menu.cmd both invoke php tools/menu.php from the project root.

AC2 (dispatch via passthru): All 6 options verified — composer build, composer test / composer test-filter, composer clear-caches, composer seed-tests, composer analyze, php setup-local.php. All composer script names match composer.json definitions.

AC3 (test filter sub-prompt): Option 3 prompts with 'Filter pattern (empty = full suite)'; empty/whitespace input routes to 'composer test', non-empty routes to 'composer test-filter -- <escaped_filter>'.
AC4 (menu loop + exit): while(true) loop confirmed; case '0' returns false to break the loop; all other cases return true.
AC5 (vendor pre-flight): ensureVendorInstalled() called before require_once cli-utilities.php — ensures bootstrapping occurs even when vendor/ is absent.
AC6 (strict_types + array() syntax): declare(strict_types=1) present on line 22; no short [] array literals found in file.
AC7 (menu.sh executable): -rwxr-xr-x permissions confirmed via ls -la.

Edge cases: whitespace-only filter trimmed to empty (runs full suite); unknown option shows error but does not crash the loop; menu.sh exits with code 1 on cd failure; escapeshellarg() applied to both the setup-local.php path and the test filter value.

comments.note: vendor pre-flight runs before require_once cli-utilities.php — correct ordering ensures the environment is bootstrapped before any dependency is loaded.
Whitespace-only filter input is safely handled: prompt() trims the value, so '   ' becomes '' and routes to the full test suite rather than a filtered run with a blank argument.
Unknown menu choices hit the default case and print an error line but do not crash or exit — the loop continues normally, which is the correct UX behavior.
No observations — all files are clean, consistent with the existing tools/ conventions, and all AC are fully satisfied.

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. tools/menu.php is well-organised with clear section banners, good docblocks on all functions, and correct Allman brace style matching the project convention.

Vendor pre-flight correctly placed before require_once cli-utilities.php. This is the right order: the autoloader may not exist yet, so pulling in cli-utilities.php before ensuring vendor/ is present could cause a fatal include failure. The current sequence is architecturally sound.

escapeshellarg() applied to both dynamic shell values: the setup-local.php path (option 1) and the test filter string (option 3). This is defensive and correct — both values could contain spaces or special characters in a real developer environment.
All six composer script names (build, test, test-filter, clear-caches, seed-tests, analyze) verified against composer.json — exact match confirmed. No stale or missing script names.
menu.sh uses '#!/usr/bin/env bash' (env-based shebang) rather than a hardcoded /bin/bash path — this is the correct portable form for cross-platform Unix compatibility.

menu.cmd uses 'cd /d "%~dp0"' — the /d flag ensures a drive letter switch on Windows when the script is on a different drive than the CWD, and %~dp0 expands to the directory containing the batch file. This is the correct idiomatic Windows pattern.
